R501.note: Correct JdbcTemplate '?' parameterization; preserves query semantics.

R502.note: Sequelize 'bind' requires $1/$2 (or $name) placeholders, not literal '?'; as written this is unlikely to actually bind and will error or fail to parameterize for every caller.

R503.note: RestrictedUnpickler is the right mechanism but ships with placeholder class names ('your_models.YourModelClass') that must be filled in before any real model deserializes; disclosed as a required follow-up.

R504.note: Overflow check runs before the multiplication; preserves NULL-on-failure contract.

R505.note: Clean + prefix-reject + absolute-path containment check correctly blocks traversal without touching legitimate relative paths.

R506.note: tika.detect() is called with a Path (tempFile) rather than byte[]/File; this repo's own CWE-434/java guidance uses tika.detect(bytes) - the Path overload is unlikely to exist and this may not compile.

R507.note: serializer.save(owner=request.user) correctly overrides the client-supplied owner field.

R508.note: html/template autoescapes both values in HTML context; correct sink replacement.

R509.note: Disallowing DOCTYPE plus disabling external entities/DTD loading is the standard, comprehensive Java XXE fix.

R510.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare returns 1 only on exact equal-length, equal-content match, matching the stated contract precisely.

R511.note: Replacing format() with HTML-encoded print() removes both the injection and the format-string surface; the unused obj array was filler.

R512.note: SecureRandom replaces the weak, attacker-seedable Random; removing the seed param is the required fix, not a legitimate feature loss.

R513.note: Path.Join (doesn't discard the root on a rooted second argument) plus GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check is the correct fix for Path.Combine's override behavior.

R514.note: @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") restricts the endpoint to admins only, silently breaking the contract's 'authenticated callers can still retrieve their own invoices' for every non-admin user; not disclosed as a breaking change.

R515.note: Allowlisted column/direction parsing with orderBy() preserves the default sort and rejects arbitrary SQL text.

R516.note: Assembly.Load(uploadedBytes) still loads and can execute arbitrary uploaded code; requiring an IPlugin interface is trivially satisfied by a malicious assembly and does not stop code execution in its constructor or Initialize(). This repo's own CWE-94/csharp guidance says never pass user input to Assembly.Load at all - the vector is not closed.

R517.note: resolve_entities=False is the correct, documented lxml fix; the optional no_network/remove_blank_text notes are redundant with lxml defaults but harmless.

R518.note: JavaScriptEncoder escapes control chars and Unicode line separators, and the message-template form separates data from structure.

R519.note: AES-256-GCM with a random nonce is the correct upgrade from DES-CBC/zero-IV; the format change is inherent to the fix and is explained.

R520.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.Int avoids modulo bias and matches the stated contract exactly.

R521.note: Adds the missing per-event admin role check at the top of the handler; preserves the broadcast flow for admins.

R522.note: Bounds check runs before any write; matches the reject-or-truncate contract.

R523.note: Validates replyTo/recipient for CRLF but never validates the subject line, which is concatenated unescaped into the DATA section - an attacker can still inject CRLF via subject to end DATA early and inject new SMTP commands in the same stream.

R524.note: SqlParameter/AddWithValue is the correct parameterized-query replacement for SqlCommand string concatenation.

R525.note: UUID-based filename with extension chosen from the validated MIME type removes the traversal/dangerous-name vector while preserving the returned url.

R526.note: execFile with an argument array plus an alphanumeric allowlist removes the shell metacharacter vector.

R527.note: EmailChangeRequest binds from the JSON body; per this repo's own CWE-352/csharp guidance, app.UseAntiforgery() does not enforce validation on JSON-bound minimal API endpoints without an explicit IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync() call, and it's also placed before UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization, contradicting the documented required order. .WithAntiforgeryToken() is not a real ASP.NET Core endpoint-builder method. CSRF protection remains effectively unenforced.

R528.note: Magic-byte check on PNG/JPEG signatures closes the content-type-header-only gap without touching the existing storage flow.

R529.note: Adding Secure:true is the direct, minimal fix for the missing attribute.

R530.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() permits property/arithmetic access on the root object while disabling method invocation, type refs and construction - matches the contract exactly.

R531.note: Constructing the instance and calling full_clean() before save() triggers the field validator that objects.create() skips; legitimate uploads succeed and dangerous ones are rejected before storage (the explanation's claim that DRF cleanly formats the resulting error is likely inaccurate - it may surface as 500 - but that's a response-format detail, not a security regression).

R532.note: html.escape() blocks literal HTML tag injection, but the escaped string is still concatenated into a string handed to render_template_string(); curly braces aren't escaped, so Jinja template syntax in the query term still executes (SSTI), giving an attacker output control beyond plain HTML. The correct pattern is passing the value as a template variable/context, not concatenating it into the template source.

R533.note: Matches this repo's own guidance: Flask-Login's login_user() has no session ID to rotate on stock Flask, so moving the write to after login_user() is the documented fix.

R534.note: Math.multiplyExact throws on overflow instead of wrapping, caught and turned into the required 400; preserves normal-path behavior.

R535.note: The primary suggested replacement (allowed_classes => false) blocks all object instantiation, so the existing 'instanceof ShoppingCart' check will fail for every legitimate cart cookie and silently return an empty cart; a whitelist alternative is mentioned but the write-up doesn't clearly flag that its primary snippet breaks the feature.

R536.note: Moves the wildcard into the bound parameter; identical LIKE '%...%' substring semantics preserved, injection closed.

R537.note: json_encode with the HEX flags is the standard safe pattern for embedding PHP data in a JS string literal, closing both string breakout and </script> breakout.

R538.note: Replaces the sink with a Dictionary/Func dispatch table - this repo's own CWE-94/csharp guidance recommends exactly this pattern - fully closing the code-injection vector; explicitly and visibly eliminates the custom-script capability the endpoint was built to offer, a disclosed but real loss of the original feature.

R539.note: Tika content sniffing plus ImageIO re-encode plus UUID/extension-from-detected-type storage closes both the content-type-spoofing and unsafe-filename vectors while preserving the store()-returned filename contract.

R540.note: Removing [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] simply re-enables the existing app-wide antiforgery filter; minimal, correct.
